name: SikaSeal Kitchen and Bathroom
paste:
SIKASEAL® KITCHEN AND BATHROOM: SPECIFICATION CLAUSE SET

Source: SikaSeal® Kitchen and Bathroom, April 2023, Version 03.01 (https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/a/sikaseal_kitchenandbathroom.pdf)
Draft for specifier review. Wording, values and standards are quoted from that data sheet; where it is silent the clause says 'Refer to manufacturer.' Confirm the current edition before issue.

1 SCOPE
1.1 Work included. Provide SikaSeal® Kitchen and Bathroom where documented, installed or applied in accordance with this clause and the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (April 2023, Version 03.01).
1.2 Product description.
    - SikaSeal® Kitchen and Bathroom is a one-component, neutral curing, low odour silicone sealant with excellent adhesion.
    - SikaSeal® Kitchen and Bathroom cures through the absorption of atmospheric moisture to give a tough but flexible waterproof seal.
1.3 Intended uses stated by the manufacturer.
    - Kitchen
    - Bathrooms
    - Showers
    - Tiled wet areas
    - Benchtops
    - Basins
    - Baths
    - Toilets
    - Around Splashbacks
    - Around plumbing fixtures and penetrations
    - General interior & exterior sealing around the home
1.4 Limits of use. Observe the manufacturer's limitations stated in clause 4.7.

2 MATERIALS
2.1 Product. SikaSeal® Kitchen and Bathroom
    - Product type as printed on the data sheet: 1-component neutral cure wet area silicone sealant
    - Supplier as printed on the data sheet: Sika Australia Pty Limited, ABN 12 001 342 329, aus.sika.com, Tel: 1300 22 33 48
2.2 Approvals, certificates and standards stated by the manufacturer. Refer to manufacturer. The data sheet reviewed (April 2023, Version 03.01) has no approvals, certificates or standards section.
2.3 Characteristics stated by the manufacturer.
    - Neutral cure
    - Excellent adhesion to most common construction materials such as: glass, enamel, ceramics, tiles, most metal*, most plastic, rubber, concrete and grouts
    - Non-sag
    - Great tooling characteristics
    - Mould resistance
    - Interior and exterior usage
    - Fast curing
    - Minimum movement capability ±25%
    - High temperature resistance (-40°c to +150°c)
    *Not for use on all metal substrates i.e. copper.
    -See Important Considerations below prior to use.
2.4 Composition, appearance and supply.
    - Composition: Neutral cure silicone
    - Colour: White, Translucent, Mid Grey, Off White, Black, Stone, Pewter, Grey, Charcoal, Brown, Beige, Almond Ivory, Alabaster
2.5 Density.
    | Translucent | ~1.01 kg/l |
    | Colours | ~1.4 kg/l |
2.6 Properties stated by the manufacturer.
    - Service temperature: -40°c to +150°c
2.7 Shore A hardness.
    | Translucent | ~25 |
    | Colours | ~47 |
2.8 Secant tensile modulus.
    | Translucent @23°c | 0.45 N/mm² |
    | Colours @23°c | 0.62 N/mm² |
2.9 Elongation at break.
    | Translucent | ~250% |
    | Colours | ~310% |
2.10 Movement capability.
    | Translucent | ±25% |
    | Colours | ±50% |
2.11 Joint design. The joint width must be designed to suit the joint movement required and the movement capability of the sealant. The joint width shall be ≥ 6 mm and ≤ 45 mm. The joint depth shall be ≥ 6 mm and ≤ 15 mm. A width to depth ratio of 2:1 must be maintained (for exceptions, see table below). Typical joint dimensions.
    | Joint Width (mm) | Joint Depth (mm) | Joint Length /600 ml ssg |
    | 6 | 4 | 25 mm |
    | 9 | 5 | 13 mm |
    | 12 | 6 | 8 mm |
    All joints must be correctly designed and dimensioned in accordance with the relevant standards, before their construction. The basis for calculation of the necessary joint widths are the type of structure and its dimensions, the technical values of the adjacent building materials and the joint sealing material, as well as the specific exposure of the building and the joints. For larger joints please contact Sika technical service.
2.12 Packaging, shelf life and storage.
    - Packaging: 300ml cartridges
    - Shelf life: 12 months from date of production if stored in undamaged and unopened original sealed containers.
    - Storage conditions: Storage in dry conditions and protected from direct sunlight at temperatures between +5°C and +25°C.

3 SUBSTRATE PREPARATION
3.1 General. Prepare substrates in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (April 2023, Version 03.01) and the requirements below. Inspect the substrate against these requirements before application.
3.2 Substrate preparation.
    - The substrate must be clean, dry, sound and free from oils, grease, dust, cement laitance and loose or friable particles. For optimum adhesion, joint durability and critical, high performance applications such as joints on multi-storey buildings, highly stressed joints, extreme weather exposure or water immersion/exposure. The following priming and/or pre-treatment procedures must be followed:
    - Non-porous substrates
    - Float glass, coated glass, anodised aluminium and stainless steel must be pre-treated using Sika® Aktivator-205 or Sika® Aktivator-100. Powder coated and PVDF coated metals must be pre-treated using Sika® Aktivator-205. For more details such as application and flash-off times, refer to the most recent Product Data Sheet of the respective pre-treatment product. Porous substrates
    - Concrete, aerated concrete and cement based renders, mortars and bricks must be primed using Sika® Primer-3 N. For more details such as application and flash-off times, refer to the most recent Product Data Sheet of the respective pre-treatment product. Adhesion tests on project specific substrates must be performed and procedures agreed with all parties before full project application. Contact Sika Technical Services for additional information. Note: Primers and activators are adhesion promoters and not an alternative to improve poor preparation/cleaning of the joint surface. Primers also improve the long term adhesion performance of the sealed joint.

4 APPLICATION
4.1 General. Apply in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (April 2023, Version 03.01) and the requirements below.
4.2 Application data.
    - Curing rate: Approximately 3-4mm per 24 hours @ 23°C/50% r.h.
4.3 Tack free time.
    | Translucent | ~5-10 minutes |
    | Colours | ~40 minutes |
4.4 Application method / tools.
    - Masking
    - It is recommended to use masking tape where neat or exact joint lines are required. Remove the tape within the skin time after finishing.
4.5 Application method / tools - Joint Backing.
    - After the required substrate preparation, insert a suitable backing rod to the required depth.
    - Priming
    - If required, prime the joint surfaces as recommended in substrate preparation. Avoid excessive application of primer to avoid causing puddles at the base of the joint.
    - Application
    - SikaSeal® Kitchen and Bathroom is supplied ready to use. Prepare the end of the foil pack or cartridge, insert into the sealant gun and fit the nozzle. Extrude SikaSeal® Kitchen and Bathroom into the joint ensuring that it comes into full contact with the sides of the joint and avoiding any air entrapment.
    - Finishing
    - As soon as possible after application, sealant must be firmly tooled against the joint sides to ensure adequate adhesion and a smooth finish. Use a compatible water based non-staining tooling agent (e.g. Sika® Tooling Agent N) to smooth the joint surface. Do not use tooling products containing solvents.
4.6 Cleaning of equipment. Clean all tools and application equipment with Sika® Remover-208 immediately after use. Hardened material can only be removed mechanically. For cleaning skin, use Sika® Cleaning Wipes-100.
4.7 Limitations and important considerations.
    - When applying sealant into a previously silicone sealed joint, ensure all residue is removed from joint.
    - Colour variations may occur due to the exposure in service to chemicals, high temperatures and/or UV-radiation (especially with white colour shade). This effect is aesthetic and does not adversely influence the technical performance or durability of the product.
    - The complete absence of UV may cause light coloured silicone (especially white) to discolour, this effect is aesthetic and does not adversely influence the technical performance or durability of the product.
    - SikaSeal® Kitchen and Bathroom cannot be overpainted.
    - Do not use on natural stone.
    - Do not use on bituminous substrates, natural rubber or any building materials which might leach oils, plasticisers or solvents that could degrade the sealant. EPDM or other gaskets in direct contact with SikaSeal® Kitchen and Bathroom have to be tested for compatibility prior to application. For specific advice contact Sika technical services.
    - Pre-test should be performed prior to use on prestressed polyacrylate and polycarbonate as it may cause environmental stress cracking (crazing).
    - Pre-test in an inconspicuous area prior to use in application on porous material such as concrete to ensure the product does not stain the substrate.
    - Do not use SikaSeal® Kitchen and Bathroom in areas which are exposed to strong oxidising acids (e.g. nitric acid) and bases.
    - Do not use to seal joints in or around swimming pools.
    - Do not use for joints under water pressure or permanent water immersion.
    - Do not use SikaSeal® Kitchen and Bathroom in totally confined spaces as it requires atmospheric moisture to cure.
    - Do not use for medical or pharmaceutical applications.

5 QUALITY CONTROL AND TESTING
5.1 Hold point. Before each application, measure and record the conditions in clause 5.2 and compare them with the manufacturer's limits. HOLD POINT: do not proceed until the Superintendent has released the hold point.
5.2 Ambient air temperature. +5 °C min./+40 °C max.
5.3 Substrate temperature. +5 °C min./+40 °C max. Minimum +3 °C above dew point temperature
5.4 Conditions stated in the limitations. Also stated in the data sheet limitations (clause 4.7):
    - Colour variations may occur due to the exposure in service to chemicals, high temperatures and/or UV-radiation (especially with white colour shade). This effect is aesthetic and does not adversely influence the technical performance or durability of the product.
    - Do not use SikaSeal® Kitchen and Bathroom in totally confined spaces as it requires atmospheric moisture to cure.
5.5 Trials, test areas and compatibility checks stated by the manufacturer.
    - Pre-test in an inconspicuous area prior to use in application on porous material such as concrete to ensure the product does not stain the substrate.
5.6 Basis of the stated values. All technical data stated in this Product Data Sheet are based on laboratory tests. Actual measured data may vary due to circumstances beyond our control.
5.7 Other tests. For any test method, sampling frequency or acceptance criterion not stated in this clause: refer to manufacturer and the project specification.

6 WARRANTY AND DOCUMENTATION
6.1 Documents to be obtained and submitted. Obtain the current issue of each document before ordering and submit it with the product submission. Documents are listed as published on the manufacturer's website.
    - Product Data Sheet: SikaSeal® Kitchen and Bathroom, April 2023, Version 03.01, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/a/sikaseal_kitchenandbathroom.pdf
    - Safety Data Sheet: Sikaseal Kitchen and Bathroom, version 22/12/2022, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/o/SikaSeal%20Kitchen%20&%20Bathroom%20GHS7.pdf
    - Safety Data Sheet: SDS SikaSeal® KITCHEN AND BATHROOM, version 15/09/2025, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/q/sds-sikaseal-kitchenandbathroom.pdf
6.2 Ecology, health and safety. For information and advice on the safe handling, storage and disposal of chemical products, users shall refer to the most recent Safety Data Sheet (SDS) containing physical, ecological, toxicological and other safety-related data.
6.3 Warranty. Obtain any product or installation warranty in writing from the manufacturer or its authorised applicator and file it with the project records. Warranty terms: refer to manufacturer.
    - Legal notes: In practice, the differences in materials, substrates and actual site conditions are such that no warranty in respect of merchantability or of fitness for a particular purpose, nor any liability arising out of any legal relationship whatsoever, can be inferred either from this information, or from any written recommendations, or from any other advice offered.
6.4 Local restrictions. Please note that as a result of specific local regulations the declared data for this product may vary from country to country. Please consult the local Product Data Sheet for the exact product data.
6.5 Application records. Record the product name, batch numbers, dates, areas treated and the conditions measured under clause 5.2, and include the records in the project documentation.
